Inspected the returned Qwen3.5 cache semantics and confirmed a deeper baseline blocker: the model uses a hybrid stack with linear_attention on 24 of 32 layers and full_attention on only 8 layers, so runtime state includes convolution and recurrent caches in addition to ordinary KV tensors. progressNotes: Completed the first follow-up route run on March 30, 2026 using Route B (State -> direct KV) for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples.

Route B direct-KV produced F1 0.4951 and TTFT 54.22 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 45.42 ms in the same run. This corresponds to about 71.3% F1 retention at 1.194x TTFT versus full consumer.

Relative to the clean original semantic patch rerun, Route B improved the normalized TTFT ratio from 1.290x to 1.194x but did not rescue the claim because quality was slightly worse than the clean semantic patch and much worse than reuse_fallback.

Completed the second follow-up route run on March 30, 2026 using pure Route A (State -> State -> native Wk/Wv -> KV) for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. The Route A reuse_patch path produced F1 0.0000 and TTFT 54.55 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 39.94 ms in the same run. This corresponds to 0.0% F1 retention at 1.366x TTFT versus full consumer, so Route A is clearly worse than both the clean original semantic patch rerun and Route B direct-KV on this pair.

Completed the third follow-up route run on March 30, 2026 using Route C (State -> State -> suffix recompute on B) for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on CMRC with 200 samples. Using the Route A state-only patch checkpoint plus a one-layer default short recompute in strict runtime, reuse_patch_recompute produced F1 0.6195 and TTFT 64.71 ms, versus full-consumer F1 0.6945 and TTFT 37.09 ms in the same run. This corresponds to 89.2% F1 retention at 1.745x TTFT versus full consumer. Route C therefore repaired the pure Route A quality collapse but still failed the claim and was dominated by same-run reuse_fallback, which was both faster and more accurate.

Completed an aligned first-token timing rerun for the Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 Route C setup on March 30, 2026. When full_consumer is measured with the same cache-based first-token path as transfer methods, full_consumer.decode_first_ms rises to 24.42 ms, matching the 23.2 to 23.4 ms range of the transfer modes. Under this aligned definition, full_consumer records F1 0.6904 at TTFT 69.33 ms, reuse_patch_recompute records F1 0.6195 at TTFT 69.83 ms, and reuse_fallback remains the strongest practical path at F1 0.6605 and TTFT 60.99 ms. This confirms that the earlier full_consumer decode-first advantage was a measurement-boundary artifact rather than a true per-token decode advantage.

Completed matched first-token timing reruns for the clean original semantic patch setup and the Route B direct-KV setup on March 30, 2026. Across clean original, Route B, and Route C, full_consumer.decode_first_ms moves from near-zero under the old definition to roughly 24.4 to 27.6 ms under the cache-based aligned definition, matching the 23.2 to 23.8 ms range of the transfer paths. This confirms that the earlier full_consumer first-token advantage was a measurement-boundary artifact. Under aligned TTFT, clean original reuse_patch reaches 65.52 ms with F1 0.5010, Route B reuse_patch reaches 55.61 ms with F1 0.4951, and Route C reuse_patch_recompute reaches 69.83 ms with F1 0.6195, while reuse_fallback remains the strongest practical path across all aligned reruns.

Set aligned TTFT as the default local measurement convention for the Qwen3-1.7B route-evaluation configs by enabling runtime_eval.align_full_consumer_first_decode in the Route A, Route B, and Route C config files. Future local reruns now compare full_consumer and transfer methods under the same cache-based first-decode boundary by default.

Completed strict no-fallback reruns for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B-bf16 on March 31, 2026 using a route with fallback_layers removed and eval configs with run_reuse_fallback=false. Route A reuse_patch reached F1 0.0000 at 33.76 ms TTFT versus same-run full_consumer 73.14 ms; Route B reuse_patch reached F1 0.0000 at 35.69 ms versus full_consumer 86.99 ms; Route C reuse_patch_recompute reached F1 0.0000 at 46.05 ms versus full_consumer 66.76 ms. This confirms that all three routes fail under the user's no-fallback definition on the runnable near-pair.

Completed fresh strict self-self all-reuse reruns on March 31, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B with all 28 layers forced to reuse and no patch, fallback, or recompute. The grouped group_size=4 checkpoint again collapsed at F1 0.0019 on 50 CMRC samples, while the layerwise group_size=1 checkpoint reached F1 0.7372 versus same-run full_consumer 0.7375. Additional reconstruction diagnostics showed large grouped relative L2 errors and localized the implementation problem to the grouped shared-z reuse codec rather than route assembly. For current Qwen3-1.7B diagnostics, layerwise reuse is now the recommended default baseline.

Completed a batched layerwise reuse acceleration rerun on April 1, 2026 for the strict Qwen3-1.7B self-self all-reuse route. The new strict_runtime fast path batches all 28 single-layer reuse groups into one encode/decode path without changing payload size (41.32 MB, compression ratio 1.0). This preserved reuse_only F1 0.7372 while reducing TTFT from 65.48 ms to 40.67 ms and reducing encode_ms from 26.86 ms to 0.88 ms; same-run full_consumer was 45.05 ms. This localizes the previous reuse_only overhead to the serial per-layer encode/decode loop rather than to transfer, which remained about 1.73 ms.

Completed an aligned self-self layerwise reuse rerun on April 1, 2026 using a dedicated eval config with runtime_eval.align_full_consumer_first_decode=true. This moved full_consumer.decode_first_ms from the old unaligned 1.18 ms to 26.51 ms, close to reuse_only.decode_first_ms 25.26 ms, confirming that the earlier first-token gap was only a measurement-boundary artifact. The same rerun also exposed a remaining timing-accounting issue in the reuse path: transfer_ms is still a modeled bandwidth term, while rebuild_ms still includes the real z.to(consumer_device) cross-device copy inside the decoder-side reconstruction path, so transport is semantically double-counted until rebuild is split into copy time and pure decode/materialization time.

Completed a timing-accounting cleanup for the strict self-self layerwise reuse path on April 1, 2026. The runtime now records the real in-process z.to(consumer_device) movement as staging_copy_ms, keeps transfer_ms as the modeled bandwidth term, and treats rebuild_ms as pure consumer-side decode/materialization compute only. A corrected aligned rerun then reduced reuse_only TTFT from the old double-counted 34.51 ms to 29.68 ms, with encode_ms 0.42, transfer_ms 1.73, staging_copy_ms 6.34, rebuild_ms 2.02, and decode_first_ms 25.50. This confirms that the previous reuse_only accounting had been overstating TTFT by about 5 to 6 ms.

Changed the strict self-self layerwise reuse runtime again on April 1, 2026 so that transfer_ms now reports the actual measured local cross-device copy time rather than the modeled bandwidth term, while modeled_transfer_ms preserves the old paper-style reference. Under the user's default no-fallback policy, the latest rerun at C:/Users/mql16/Desktop/SCD-ICML/tmp_github_branch_update/scd-new-branch-staging/Experiment/analysis/remote_artifacts/qwen17_self_allreuse_layerwise_actualtransfer_nofallback_50_20260401/summary.json reports full_consumer at F1 0.7462 and TTFT 85.82 ms, versus reuse_only at F1 0.7372 and TTFT 39.78 ms with encode_ms 0.42, transfer_ms 6.46 actual, modeled_transfer_ms 1.73, rebuild_ms 7.17, and decode_first_ms 25.74. This is now the default headline artifact for the self-self layerwise reuse route.

Updated the local strict runtime on April 1, 2026 to simplify future latency accounting further. New summaries will no longer emit modeled_transfer_ms, and rebuild_ms will be split into rebuild_prep_ms, rebuild_decode_core_ms, rebuild_rerope_ms, and rebuild_materialize_ms so the remaining consumer-side bottleneck can be diagnosed directly on the next rerun. Historical artifacts are kept unchanged.

Ran a fresh self-self layerwise reuse_only rerun on April 1, 2026 after adding rebuild sub-term accounting. The new artifact at C:/Users/mql16/Desktop/SCD-ICML/tmp_github_branch_update/scd-new-branch-staging/Experiment/analysis/remote_artifacts/qwen17_self_allreuse_layerwise_rebuildsplit_50_20260401/summary.json reports reuse_only F1 0.7372 and TTFT 34.06 ms with encode_ms 0.42, transfer_ms 6.32, rebuild_ms 2.30, and decode_first_ms 25.03. The rebuild split shows prep 0.10 ms, decode core 0.41 ms, re_rope 1.05 ms, and materialize 0.74 ms, so the remaining rebuild bottleneck is mainly K re-rope plus final dtype/contiguous materialization rather than the actual z-to-KV matrix decode.

Switched the local qwen17 route wrappers to default to a layerwise reuse checkpoint path instead of the older grouped ckpt_reuse_seed42 baseline. Added Experiment/core_code/run_ser_qwen17_reuse_layerwise.sh as the explicit near-pair layerwise reuse training entrypoint, and made the Route A/B/C wrapper scripts fail fast if the layerwise checkpoint is missing rather than silently reusing the grouped baseline.

Completed fresh strict self-self patch diagnostics on March 31, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B using the healthy layerwise reuse baseline plus a direct-KV patch checkpoint trained on all 28 layers. The strict all-patch route collapsed to F1 0.0049 at 62.38 ms TTFT versus same-run full_consumer 0.7375 at 43.67 ms and same-run reuse_only 0.7372 at 55.34 ms. Excluding layer 0 from the patch route raised F1 only to 0.0508 at 71.02 ms TTFT. Training logs showed a layer-0 patch_kv_error explosion to about 6.8e6, but the excl0 rerun confirms the patch path is broadly unhealthy rather than only suffering from a single-layer bug.

Completed a Qwen-specific self-self patch repair on March 31, 2026 under strict no-fallback, no-recompute settings. The earlier collapse was traced to two implementation bugs: pair capture silently truncated training prefixes to 256 tokens, and the Qwen direct-KV path fit and replayed the wrong key formulation. After fixing max-length precedence, adding fit mode direct_kv_knorm_v1, and switching runtime to consumer-native rotary, the all-28-layer patch rerun still failed at F1 0.0119 and TTFT 75.35 ms, but the excl0 route (patch layers 1..27) reached F1 0.7425, EM 0.44, and TTFT 88.10 ms on 50 CMRC samples. For current Qwen3-1.7B self-self experiments, the default patch setting is now direct_kv_knorm_v1 with consumer-native rotary and patch_layers 1..27; layer 0 remains the only unresolved blocker.

Completed a dedicated layer-0 control audit on March 31, 2026 to determine whether the remaining self-self patch failure came from runtime semantics or from the learned layer-0 translator itself. Tensor diagnostics showed xnorm_a.0 and xnorm_b.0 are exactly identical on all 50 samples, while consumer-native k_proj/v_proj plus k_norm and native rotary reconstruct the true layer-0 KV almost exactly (K rel-MSE about 5.59e-6, V rel-MSE about 4.79e-6). In contrast, the learned layer-0 direct_kv_knorm_v1 translator is catastrophically wrong (K rel-MSE about 1.49, V rel-MSE about 2.58e7). A strict route-level control with only layer 0 patched confirmed the same conclusion: oracle_kv_patchonly on layer 0 matched reuse_only at F1 0.7372, while learned reuse_patch on layer 0 alone collapsed to F1 0.0124. This localizes the remaining issue to the trained layer-0 Wk/Wv solution rather than to self-self capture semantics or runtime cache overwrite.

Completed a strict self-self nonlinear follow-up on March 31, 2026 by switching the patch translator to the existing xnorm_semantic_v1 PatchMLP route (state_target_space=xnorm, patch_apply_mode=overwrite, lambda_h=1, lambda_k=lambda_v=lambda_sem=0). Unlike the repaired direct_kv_knorm_v1 excl0 path, this nonlinear route failed completely: all-28-layer reuse_patch reached F1 0.0000 at 102.16 ms TTFT and the excl0 route also stayed at F1 0.0000 at 126.85 ms on 50 CMRC samples. Checkpoint metrics showed low hidden MSE only for layers 0..2, while deeper layers diverged sharply, so the current MLP formulation is not a viable rescue and the direct_kv_knorm_v1 excl0 path remains the only healthy self-self patch result.

Completed a stronger direct-KV residual nonlinear follow-up on March 31, 2026 for Qwen3-1.7B -> Qwen3-1.7B self-self. The new fit mode direct_kv_knorm_residual_mlp_v1 kept the repaired linear direct_kv_knorm_v1 path on all layers and added a 4096-wide 4-block residual MLP only on layer 0, which is the sole remaining broken layer. The first remote run exposed a preload device-placement bug (CPU xnorm_b projected with cuda:1 weights); that bug was fixed locally and on ser, and the v2 rerun completed successfully. The result was still negative: all-28-layer reuse_patch reached F1 0.0087 at 193.11 ms TTFT, the dedicated layer-0-only control reached F1 0.0113 at 177.57 ms while oracle_kv_patchonly remained healthy at F1 0.7372, and the excl0 route simply preserved the earlier healthy linear result at F1 0.7425 but slowed to 122.10 ms TTFT. Residual training barely reduced layer-0 error (base_k_rel_mse about 1.213e7 -> 1.199e7, base_v_rel_mse about 2.330e7 -> 2.184e7), so this stronger nonlinear route also fails to rescue layer 0 or improve the usable excl0 operating point.

Added a consolidated status memo on March 31, 2026 at C:/Users/mql16/Desktop/SCD-ICML/tmp_github_branch_update/scd-new-branch-staging/Experiment/analysis/current_progress_and_blockers_20260331.md. The memo now summarizes the current evidence boundary across Qwen3.5 hybrid-cache blocking, runnable Qwen near-pair no-fallback failures, grouped self-self reuse invalidity, the repaired direct_kv_knorm_v1 excl0 self-self patch result, and the failure of both nonlinear follow-ups: the existing PatchMLP route and the stronger direct-KV residual MLP route.

Completed the route-2 self-self patch repair on March 31, 2026 by switching the broken layer-0 translator from direct KV regression to an identity-anchored hidden residual route, xnorm_nativekv_residual_mlp_v1. This parameterization predicts xb_hat = xa + delta_h only on layer 0 and then lets the consumer derive KV natively through k_proj/v_proj, k_norm, and native rotary. The result resolves the earlier layer-0 quality failure: the strict all-28-layer reuse_patch route reached F1 0.7700, EM 0.46, and TTFT 200.01 ms on 50 CMRC samples, while the dedicated layer-0-only control matched reuse_only and oracle_kv_patchonly at F1 0.7372. Saved training metrics show the selected layer-0 solution stays at identity initialization (base_h_rel_mse 0.0, base_k_rel_mse about 1.43e-11, base_v_rel_mse about 1.55e-11), which confirms the old collapse came from direct-KV parameterization rather than runtime cache overwrite. The remaining bottleneck is efficiency, not correctness: patch_infer_ms dominates TTFT because runtime still executes the residual MLP even though the chosen checkpoint is effectively identity.

Completed a runtime-only follow-up for the self-self route-2 patch repair on March 31, 2026 by adding an identity fast path for xnorm_nativekv_residual_mlp_v1 on ser. The runtime now checks whether the loaded layer-0 residual module has zero delta_h_head weights and bias and, if so, skips the residual MLP forward while still applying consumer-native k_proj/v_proj, k_norm, and native rotary. This preserves correctness and reduces latency on the routes that actually use layer 0: the strict all-28-layer reuse_patch run stayed at F1 0.7700 and EM 0.46 while TTFT fell from 200.01 ms to 167.74 ms and patch_infer_ms fell from 132.23 ms to 97.44 ms; the dedicated layer-0-only control stayed at F1 0.7372 while TTFT fell from 193.12 ms to 140.55 ms and patch_infer_ms fell from 127.91 ms to 74.26 ms. The remaining bottleneck is no longer the useless residual MLP itself but the consumer-native hidden-to-KV projection path.
